texts.label: footnote
texts.orig: To construct a basis-set B which has a given set P as a subset we proceed in the following way. We well-order the continuum K in such a way that the numbers of P precede all other numbers. The set (K-P) is not empty, and since the set P is not the entire basis-set of K, there must be a first number a1 of (K-P) which cannot be represented by numbers of P in a linear way. If we consider the set P1-P+a1 and reason in the same way as above, we obtain a basis-set B of the continuum K. See also M. Kormes, Treatise on basis-sets.
